messages:
Jess: Heads-up — nightly GPU matrix is red on h100 nodes after the runtime/container image we pushed last night. Failures look like OOMs during quantized inference tests.

Omar: seeing the same. quick paste from the job log: 
```
E   RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating tensor with shape (1, 512, 4096)
RuntimeError: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
NVML: GPU 0: XID 79 (GPU page fault) at 0x7f...
```

ci-bot: job 9453 failed on pool h100-nightly (image: redwood/runtime:nightly-2026-03-16-cuda12.2). Tests: tests/inference/test_quant.py::TestKVCache::test_sequence_windows. Rerun link: https://ci.redwood.example/jobs/9453

Kate: is this after the driver bump yesterday? I thought we only bumped toolkit in the image, not the kernel driver on the host.

Omar: correct — image was rebuilt against system CUDA 12.2 libraries. Host driver got a minor roll forward on the cluster (495.xx -> 496.yy) in the same maintenance window. Could be an ABI mismatch or stricter allocation behavior.

Mike: quick parity check — the same test passes on a100-nightly and on local H100 with the old image. Fails on host H100 only. So point towards host-driver / nvidia kernel change.

Jess: can someone kick a rerun on a host with the older driver pinned? If it passes there we can pin for the pipeline. Otherwise we need to bisect image layers.

Omar: starting a diagnostic matrix: 
- rerun job 9453 on h100-olddriver pool
- run the failing pytest with -k and -s to capture memory profile
- try loading with TF_FORCE_GPU_ALLOW_GROWTH (if TF) / set PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 for isolate

ci-bot: rerun scheduled: job 9453.r1 -> pool h100-legacy-driver. Link: https://ci.redwood.example/jobs/9453/r1

Kate: also can someone grab nvml logs and dmesg around the time — XID 79 suggests a page fault. If there's a driver change that tightened permissions it could show up there.

Omar: grabbed dmesg excerpt: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (79) at 0x1234567d64e0
[ 12345.678902] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679100] docker0: port 3(veth...) entered disabled state
```

Mike: I'm going to attempt a quick local repro with the exact container and a pinned 496 driver in a VM. If I can reproduce, I'll start a git bisect on the runtime layer changes between tags nightly-2026-03-15 and nightly-2026-03-16.

Jess: thanks. If bisect points to the CUDA toolkit build step, we may need to revert the baseimage bump. If it points at our conv/attention kernel change in runtime, we should hotfix.

Omar: update: h100-legacy-driver rerun passed (9453.r1 green). So host-driver mismatch is our top suspect. 9453 (new driver) still failing.

Kate: can we pin the dedicated CI fleet to legacy driver until we have a proper plan? I'll file a ticket and request the fleet be set to 495.xx for the night.

Jess: filing PR to pin the image fallback policy to legacy-driver for the nightly job and opening an infra ticket to block the automatic driver rollout. Assigning to @Omar for bisect and @Mike for local repro.

Omar: starting a bisect across driver versions & image combos, will post minimal reproducer when done. ETA ~2-3 hours.

Mike: local repro shows same OOM with driver 496.7 + runtime-nightly-2026-03-16. With 495.2 it succeeds. Reproducer script (quick):
```bash
# run inside the container
python -u tests/inference/run_repro.py --model tiny-quant --seq 4096 --batch 1
```
Outputs memory trace and fails where the runtime requests a 2.5GB cuMemAlloc and driver returns OOM despite 10GB free.

ci-bot: monitoring label: regressions/gpu-driver-compat added to job 9453.r1 and original 9453.

Jess: good troubleshooting. Next steps: Omar to share bisect, Kate to pin fleet/drivers, I'll prepare rollback PR if needed. We'll sync async here — ping me if you need me to jump on a call. :thumbsup:

Omar: bisect update: narrowed to host driver 496.1 -> 496.7. Reproducer minimal shows kernel change in memory tracking causing earlier OOM. Opening infra ticket with logs and asking vendor.

Mike: added note to the failing test to mark flaky-if-driver>=496 until we have vendor confirmation. Will follow up with a cleanup PR to remove the temporary skip once fixed.

Kate: infra ticket created: INFRA-2142 referencing job links and dmesg. I've blocked auto-rollout and requested vendor escalation.

Jess: closing the loop — thanks all. Saving logs to the incident bucket and will convert this thread into a short postmortem if vendor confirms driver regression.

Mike: :rocket:

ci-bot: thread archived to incidents index with tag gpu-driver-compat on 1893457589.
